```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 5,
  fig.height = 7,
  out.width = "60%"
)
```

This vignette is for anyone who has a table of results per gut segment, such
as endoscopy scores, histology grades or biomarker levels, and wants a figure.
You do not need to know anything about coordinates or `ggplot2` layers.

```{r setup}
library(ggcolonviz)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 1. See which segments exist

ggcolonviz has three layouts, called *variants*:

* `"standard"`: the colon with the terminal ileum;
* `"sescd"`: the five SES-CD segments;
* `"ibd"`: the whole gastrointestinal tract, from the esophagus to the
  perianal region.

`colon_map()` draws a variant with every segment named:

```{r map}
colon_map("ibd")
```

`colon_parts()` gives the same information as a table. Use the names in the
`part` column in your own data:

```{r parts}
colon_parts("ibd")
```

## 2. Colour segments by a score

Your data needs one row per segment: a column with the segment name and a
column with the value to show. Spelling is flexible: `"TI"`,
`"terminal ileum"`, `"caecum"` and `"sigmoid colon"` are all understood.

```{r scores}
endoscopy <- data.frame(
  segment = c("TI", "caecum", "Ascending colon", "Transverse",
              "Descending", "Sigmoid colon", "Rectum"),
  ulcer_score = c(3, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2)
)

colon_plot(endoscopy, part = segment, fill = ulcer_score, variant = "ibd")
```

Segments that are not in your table are still drawn, in light grey, so the
reader can tell "not assessed" from "score 0". Use `show_all = FALSE` to hide
them.

The result is an ordinary ggplot, so titles and colour scales can be added
in the usual way:

```{r customise}
colon_plot(endoscopy, part = segment, fill = ulcer_score, variant = "ibd") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, name = "Ulcer score") +
  labs(title = "Patient 001 - baseline colonoscopy")
```

If a segment name is not recognised, you get a warning that lists the valid
names. The row is not drawn:

```{r unknown}
colon_plot(data.frame(part = c("Rectum", "Spleen")), variant = "ibd")
```

## 3. Disease location (Montreal classification)

`montreal_parts()` returns the segments covered by a Montreal code:

* L1 ileal, L2 colonic, L3 ileocolonic, L4 upper GI and p perianal for
  Crohn's disease;
* E1 proctitis, E2 left-sided and E3 extensive for ulcerative colitis.

```{r montreal}
montreal_parts("L3")

crohns <- data.frame(part = montreal_parts(c("L3", "p")), location = "Involved")
colon_plot(crohns, fill = location, variant = "ibd") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Involved = "#D7301F")) +
  labs(title = "Crohn's disease, Montreal L3 + p")
```

## 4. Several patients or visits

Add a column that identifies the panel and pass it to `facet`:

```{r visits, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%"}
visits <- rbind(
  data.frame(visit = "Week 0",  part = c("TI", "Cecum", "Rectum"), score = c(3, 2, 3)),
  data.frame(visit = "Week 12", part = c("TI", "Cecum", "Rectum"), score = c(1, 0, 1)),
  data.frame(visit = "Week 52", part = c("TI", "Cecum", "Rectum"), score = c(0, 0, 0))
)

colon_plot(visits, fill = score, facet = visit)
```

## 5. Mark lesions on a segment

`colon_position()` turns a segment name into plotting coordinates. `where`
moves the point along the segment: 0 is the left or bottom end, 1 the right or
top end.

```{r lesions}
lesions <- data.frame(
  part = c("Terminal Ileum", "Sigmoid", "Sigmoid", "Perianal"),
  where = c(0.5, 0.2, 0.8, 0.5),
  finding = c("Stricture", "Ulcer", "Ulcer", "Fistula")
)
lesions <- cbind(
  lesions,
  colon_position(lesions$part, where = lesions$where, variant = "ibd")[c("x", "y")]
)

colon_plot(lesions, variant = "ibd", label = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = lesions, aes(x = x, y = y, shape = finding), size = 3)
```

## Accepted segment names

Matching ignores case, spaces and punctuation. On top of the names returned
by `colon_parts()`, these synonyms are accepted:

| You can write | Interpreted as |
|---|---|
| TI, terminal ileum, neo-terminal ileum | Terminal Ileum (`"ibd"`) or Ileum |
| ileum | Ileum or Terminal Ileum (`"ibd"`) |
| ICV, ileocaecal valve | Ileocecal Valve |
| caecum | Cecum |
| ascending / transverse / descending / sigmoid colon | Ascending / Transverse / Descending / Sigmoid |
| right colon, left colon | Right, Left (`"sescd"`) |
| oesophagus, gastric | Esophagus, Stomach |
| anus | Anal Canal |
| perianal region, perianal disease | Perianal |
